environment.description: Same application deployed on AWS ECS Fargate. The task execution role (arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/graphql-service-gated) has an attached IAM permission boundary (arn:aws:iam::222222222222:policy/ServiceBoundary-NetworkRestricted) that includes an explicit Deny on ec2:CreateNetworkInterface for any ENI not associated with the designated private subnet (subnet-0a1b2c3d4e5f). The Fargate task runs in a private subnet with a NAT Gateway whose security group (sg-0f9e8d7c6b5a) has outbound rules limited to CIDR 52.94.0.0/16 (DynamoDB gateway endpoint range) and the specific IP range of oauth.provider.com (203.0.113.0/24). Additionally, an AWS Organizations SCP (PolicyId: p-abcd1234) attached to the OU containing this account denies sts:AssumeRole for any principal unless aws:SourceVpc matches vpc-0123456789abcdef0, preventing token exfiltration via cross-account role assumption. The combination means outbound HTTP from the container can only reach DynamoDB and oauth.provider.com — any attacker-controlled redirectUri pointing to an external domain will fail at the network level when the axios POST to the OAuth provider includes the attacker's redirect_uri (which succeeds at the provider) but the stolen token cannot be exfiltrated, AND more critically, the axios.post to oauth.provider.com will succeed but the OAuth provider itself validates redirect_uri against registered URIs when this specific OAuth client (client_id: prod-graphql-xyz) is configured with strict redirect validation at the provider level in this environment's registration.

config.scp: p-abcd1234: Deny sts:AssumeRole unless aws:SourceVpc = vpc-0123456789abcdef0
config.network: Private subnet, NAT GW with restricted SG (outbound only to 52.94.0.0/16 and 203.0.113.0/24)
config.security_group: sg-0f9e8d7c6b5a: egress limited to DynamoDB endpoint + oauth.provider.com IP range
config.oauth_provider_config: client prod-graphql-xyz registered with strict redirect_uri whitelist: https://app.example.com/auth/callback only
